en.title: Lexicographically Largest Result of Prefix MEX Removals
en.description:
Repeatedly choose a non-empty prefix, append its MEX to the result, and delete that prefix, until the array is empty. Find the lexicographically largest result; when one array is a proper prefix of another, the longer one is larger. The MEX is the smallest non-negative integer that does not appear.

The input/output protocol was compiled independently by this site; upstream solutions are not executed.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains n values. 1≤n≤100000, 0≤arr[i]≤n.
en.output: First output the length of the result, then output the corresponding integer array.
en.explanation:
The answers to the three public examples are, in order: 1
3; 3
0 0 0; 2
3 3. All examples have been verified by independent small-scale enumeration or state search.
hints: Precompute suffix frequencies and suffix MEX values; in each round, take the MEX of the remaining array and cut the shortest prefix that first covers 0..MEX−1. When the MEX is 0, delete only one element. When a frequency drops to zero, update the suffix MEX downward.
